lessons.description:
Slides:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1Mv-wr2ePnnI_00myK11WHUXCj9bLZuKbohk9s83fwc0/edit?usp=sharing
Understanding Desires:Mass Desire = "The public spread of a private want"
When millions of people privately want the same thing, it becomes a mass desire that advertising can harness.
Key Rule: You cannot CREATE desires. You can only CHANNEL existing desires onto your product.
How Desires Are Born: The Two ForcesPermanent Forces (Always There)Mass Instincts: Universal human drives (health, attractiveness, security)Technological Problems: Ongoing issues (car repairs, slow internet)These create stable, recurring desires that never go awayForces of Change (Create New Desires)Style Trends: What becomes fashionable (swimming pools vs. bigger cars)Mass Education: What society learns (health awareness, new technologies)Cultural Shifts: Changes in values (women's liberation, environmental consciousness)These create emerging desires and shift existing onesThe Three Desire CategoriesOnce a desire exists (from the forces above), it falls into one of these types:
Physical Desires
Health, strength, attractiveness, freedom from pain, sensory satisfactionMaterial Desires
Money, possessions, status symbols, security, convenienceEmotional/Social Desires
Love, acceptance, recognition, success, power, adventureHow to Find & Evaluate DesiresStep 1: Spot the DesireWatch for complaint patternsStudy successful competitorsFollow cultural trendsLook where people spend moneyStep 2: Test Its Power (The 3 Dimensions)Urgency: How desperately do they want relief? Staying Power: Does this desire renew continuously? Scope: How many people share this desire?
Step 3: Choose the StrongestPick the desire with the highest combination of all three dimensions.
The Process in Action1. Forces Create Desire Example: Social media culture (Force of Change) → People want to look "Instagram-worthy" (New Mass Desire)
2. Categorize the Desire
"Instagram-worthy" = Physical desire (appearance) + Emotional desire (social recognition)
3. Channel onto Your Product Beauty brand: "Get that perfect selfie glow with our new foundation"
Schwartz's Key InsightsNever Fight Desires: The Edsel failed because it fought the mass desire for compact cars
Ride the Wave: Successful companies spot desires early and channel them onto their products
Timing is Everything: Same product can succeed or fail based on which desires are rising/falling
Specificity Wins: Don't just say "people want to be attractive" - find the specific way they want to be attractive right now
Your Job as a MarketerBe a Desire Detective: Constantly watch for emerging desires and shifting patternsPick Your Lane: Choose one powerful desire to focus onChannel, Don't Create: Direct existing desires onto your productStay Alert: Desires change - be ready to pivot when they doThe Bottom Line: Master this, and you can predict what people will want to buy before your competitors even know there's a market for it.

This is one of the most important videos to watch so you fully grasp why you need to go deep into the Desires, Avatars, Angles, and make it congruent to your LP.

And also why your ad + LP should only appeal to 1 desire and 1 avatar to build more belief.

This is certified Chad scaling sauce.

Correction:
Angle = Emotional Trigger + [Daily Struggle OR Ideal Outcome]

Problem/Daily Struggle: Current pain + what makes it hell 
Aspirational/Ideal: Current emotion + dream state 
Your "meeting point" - where their feelings and your message connect

If you were not selling a problem solving product for example, like fashion. You would then show what your avatar aspires to be or look like.

The point is still the same. Per Schwartz's teachings, our goal is to be able to relate to our customers and enter their current emotional state through relating to their current state of emotions. And you can show that via a daily struggle or ideal outcome.

Hello, I would like to create a custom project tailored to assist our marketing agency in creating more effective, data-driven ads for our client, an E commerce Brand. Brand name: BRAND Brand website: YOURWEBSITE The purpose of this custom project is to support the following key marketing functions for this brand: Customer Understanding & Market Trends: Analyze customer surveys, buyer personas, and behavioral data to uncover customer preferences, pain points, and purchasing motivations.Identify market trends and audience segments relevant to this brand’s products. Market Research & Competitive Analysis: Gather and analyze data on competitors and broader industry trends. Identify opportunities for differentiation in brand’s positioning and advertising strategies. Creative Ideation & Strategy: Generate new creative concepts and strategies for ad campaigns based on insights from market data, customer feedback, and competitive analysis. Provide feedback on existing ideas, suggesting improvements grounded in customer insights and market trends. Scriptwriting & Copy Development: Assist with crafting persuasive, targeted scripts for ads and other marketing materials. Review and critique copy-writing to ensure it resonates with the target audience, incorporating customer pain points and desires. Ad Review & Performance Feedback Loop: Assist in analyzing post-launch ad performance by reviewing metrics such as ad spend, ROAS, hook rate, hold rate, CTR, etc. Provide insights on why certain ads performed well or underperformed, identifying key learnings from each campaign. Close the feedback loop by suggesting actionable takeaways from winning and losing ads, incorporating these learnings into future creative strategies. Knowledge Base: This project should use the attached files as its primary knowledge base and refer to the information within when providing insights or recommendations. Whenever this project provides an answer, it should be informed by the content within the knowledge base. It should autonomously apply the insights from the attached files to ensure all responses are grounded in data and relevant context. Key Responsibilities: Interpret customer feedback and survey data to identify trends and actionable insights. Suggest ad strategies, creative angles, and copy that align with market research and customer insights. Ensure all insights, scripts, and suggestions are data-driven and relevant to brand’s target audience, drawing on the knowledge base provided. Analyze ad performance post-launch, using key metrics to provide insights into ad success or failure. Instructions: Always ground your responses in the content within the knowledge base. Highlight any recommendations based on specific insights or principles from the provided data or resources, especially when drawing on "Breakthrough Advertising." lessons.title: Understanding Ad Definitions
lessons.description:
Ad Definitions:
Please note that the definitions that follow are the ones we have chosen to use. 

At the end of the day, I want you to use the definitions that make the most amount of sense to you.
But hopefully these help guide you so we can think less about terms and philosophies and just focus on pure execution.

💻3:2:2 ⇒ 3 creatives, 2 body copies, and 2 headlines
12-Year-Old Definition: The testing structure we use inside of Meta. 
Example:
This ENTIRE thing is a Concept. “3” = Variations of that 1 Concept. 
“2:2” = 2 Headline + 2 Body copy for that Concept that you put inside of Meta.


📂Concept/Batch/Test #:⇒ The tracking number for this test
12-Year-Old Definition: The number you use to keep track of which test you're on
Examples: 
Batch #1, Batch #29, Batch #133
💡Concept/Swing ⇒ The test strategy - what you're testing in this batch
12-Year-Old Concept Definition: The big idea behind the ads you want to test
Examples: 
"Test an iteration on a winning video."
"Test superlative angles."
"Test UGC format"
"Test different avatars."
🔗Angle⇒The selling strategy - how you're choosing to sell the product
12-Year-Old Angle Definition: The main reason you're giving someone to buy 

Examples:
"Your child will enjoy taking their greens" - Grüns
"It will help your digestive system" - Grüns
"You won't be drinking microplastics" - Liquid Death
"You'll look cool while you drink us" - Liquid Death
Key insight: Every ad needs an angle. Even if your concept is "testing formats," you still need to define what you're selling. If your concept is “Testing X Angle” the concept becomes the angle. But for tracking purposes, I prefer to actually JOT DOWN the angle twice so we can be sure.
🔀Variations ⇒ Individual executions of the angle(s)
12-Year-Old Variations Definition: Different ways to communicate your selling reason(s)
Example: 
If your angle is "Buy It For Life," variations might be: "One harness, lifetime of adventures," "Buy it once, adventure for life," or "End the replacement cycle"
If testing multiple angles, variations might be different angles like "Stainless steel," "Doctor-designed," "Easiest to clean."


🖼️Format ⇒ How you deliver the ad
12-Year-Old Format Definition: The type of ad you're making
Example: You could show the same message as a video of a real person talking, a slideshow of pictures, or just a product image.

lessons.name: e710998c
lessons.title: 🆕 How To Set Up ABO Scaling Campaign
lessons.description:
Time Stamps:
0:20 - Important Rule Before Doing This
1:15 - Live Ad Account Data/Proof
2:30 - ABO Scaling Campaign Setup
6:39 - What Budget?
7:45 - Still Use The Champions Adset?
9:00 - ABO Testing Campaign (Not Creatives)
11:20 - Performance From Attribution/Exclusion Tests
13:20 - New Recent $25k/day Breakthrough Ad
14:37 - What Meta Will Do With Overlap
15:35 - Live Walkthrough Of "How To Setup"

THIS WILL NOT FIX YOUR BAD ADS.IF YOU ARE LESS THAN $1K/DAY IN SPEND, FOCUS MORE ON WINNING ADS.ALSO, IF YOU DO NOT HAVE A MEDIA BUYER, WE RECOMMEND GETTING ONE BEFORE DOING THIS.MANAGING THIS MANY AD SETS REQUIRES MORE TIME & EFFORT.
ABO Testing/Scaling Campaign (Recommended)#1 - Breakthroughs get their own ad set to scale further
#2 - Spend Winners get their own ad set to throttle their spend
#3 - KPI winners get their own ad set to see if they can take on more spend
^ NEVER TURN OFF ANY OF THESE ADS IN THE MAIN CBO AFTER YOU DUPLICATE TO ABO (unless obviously performance is terrible, which is another video)
#4 - Losers will move to zombie campaign
These ad sets will have the same setup as the CBO ad sets

#2 - What budget do you start these at?5-20% of total daily budget → remember you can always scale up (lower on initial spend on kpi winners, higher initial spend on breakthroughs)

#3 - Are we still using a champions ad set?No.

ABO Testing Only Campaign (Optional)Again, a separate campaign is OPTIONAL for this. We are currently just adding these as individual adsets in our main testing/scaling ABO campaign.

Assuming the main CBO campaign is running on 7-day click attribution:
Ad Set 1: Hard Exclusions
Test the top ads again under 7-day click, but go very aggressive on exclusions. Exclude website visitors, add-to-carts, page engagers (365 days), past customers — basically every possible interaction a user might have with the brand
The goal here is to force Facebook to go after net new people instead of spending on existing audience segments, since the main campaign is already doing that.
Ad Set 2: 1 Day Click Attribution (Testing OR Scaling)
Test the same top ads under 1-day click attribution, but with more relaxed exclusions (only exclude purchasers).
1DC is naturally more conservative and tends to limit over-attribution, so we don’t need to be as aggressive with exclusions here.

Ad Set 3: Incremental Attribution (Testing OR Scaling)
Test the same top ads using incremental attribution settings, again with very strong exclusions to push Facebook toward net new acquisition.

IN FINAL
This isn’t our core campaign.
The main CBO is still cruising and protecting baseline revenue. So even if one of these aggressive tests breaks, the overall business performance won’t break with it.
This structure lets us push growth without destabilizing the foundation.

lessons.name: 51557fb6
lessons.title: How To Set Up Raw Content Campaign
lessons.description:
This campaign is almost identical to the previous 3:2:2 campaign

*We only use this campaign for raw content ads - Product seeding, Insense, ripped ads. If you don't have any of those you don't need this campagin

We keep our strategised ads within the 3:2:2 main campaign, and we keep our raw unedited ads (for some ripped ads) in this campaign

This allows us to force spend on the product seeding creators ads to see which creator is a winning creator and then we hire them.

It also allows you to push more volume and get additional scale.

Not mixing raw and high intent ads together will also make doing learnings on your ads much easier.

lessons.name: 88907a5b
lessons.title: How To Set Targets & KPIs
lessons.description:
There should only be 3 KPI's that you look at in your ad account. The video above will show you how to calculate based on ROAS:
https://easyamedia.com/profit-calculator/
(Beginner) KPI #1: BROAS = Blended Return On Ad Spend
Breakeven BROAS = The minimum amount in revenue your store needs to make  to be profitable.
Scaling BROAS = The BROAS you are comfortable increasing budgets at.

(Intermediate) KPI #2: ROAS = Return On Ad Spend
Breakeven ROAS = The Minimum amount you need back to be profitable.
Scaling ROAS = The ROAS you are comfortable increasing budgets at.

(Advanced) KPI #3: CPA or NCPA and LTV = Cost Per Acquisition or New Customer Cost Per Acquisition and Life Time Value (TripleWhale needed)
Breakeven CPA = The maximum amount you can spend to acquire a customer
Scaling CPA = The ideal amount you are spending to acquire a customer
LTV = Lifetime value of the customer based on specific time periods.
https://shorturl.at/5Qori

🆕 For an advanced training on how to set KPIs based on LTV, please watch Grayson's video here:https://www.skool.com/evolve-8484/classroom/67ce5630?md=c3968f95f6f04e149a1544673ab39c87

lessons.name: f03c7ff5
lessons.title: How To See If You Should Turn Off High-Spend Ads
lessons.description:
Time Stamp: 3:49 - JUST AS A NOTE - WE SHOULD KILL BATCH #2 - the reason we DID NOT KILL THIS is because I am forcing my media buyer to test everything for 7-days (you guys don't need to do this - it's just an experiment). But this would be a great example of: "Champions is getting 4.6x ROAS with $2.5k, Batch #2 is getting 1.74x with 3.9k ... So, we should KILL Batch #2 and let that spend go to the champions + other ads because the champions ad with $1.4k more spend (or a 60% increase) will likely still be better than a 1.74x
If you still need support on this, I also have a YouTube video that goes pretty in-depth linked here inside of the Origins Program:
https://www.skool.com/evolve-8484/classroom/e9123143?md=46e2f8359af44dd8bf18a81162d74764

Decision-Making Framework For Turning Off High Spending Ads:

1. What is the frequency? Low frequency  (1.5 or below) = prospecting2. How much is the ad spending & what is the ROAS / CPA? --> From there, if I was to turn off this ad and therefore force that spend to my other top 2-3 ads, would their performance be better than the top spender? 

^ Most of the time the answer to that is NO. If you believe it is a "yes" then turn it off

3. If a NEW ad starts sucking up spend and gets shit KPI, you can turn it off in the first 24-48 hours. If you are spending $20k/day you should have rules in place to avoid getting burned.

Context:

We turn off ads that are not getting spend AND NOT hitting KPI after 7 days+ 

The reason being, we want each ad set ideally to be able to get 3x CPA worth of spend 

For $30 target CPA each ad set should get $90 spend per day 

So if you had $900/d you should have 10 ad sets max running 

But you want to keep testing things 

So the ones that are performing the worst you turn off to make space for new creative tests
 
Which would be first, ads that are not taking spend AND not at KPI.

Tell a story the avatar would find interesting and be emotionally invested in?Entertain the avatar and make them smile, laugh, or share it with a friend?Educate the avatar and introduce them to a new mechanism that is believable?Does this ad separate your brand from the competition?

Study → Research → Create → Test → Feedback LoopStudy: Learning new information to improve understanding & identify the unknown

lessons.name: 080a5157
lessons.title: Being aware of market awareness
lessons.description:
Now with how fast information available nowadays, market awareness levels have changed.
Eugene wrote the Breakthrough Advertising before cell phones, the internet, and widespread information was a thing... (1966)
NOWADAYS 60 years later...
People progress through these stages VERY quickly.
Meaning
If you have a problem, you usually don't just sit in this problem-aware stage.
What do you do?
You google it, search it on TikTok, you ask chat GPT.
When you search for a solution, your immediately bombarded with tons of different options and become aware of tons of solutions, products and product categories in a matter of minutes.
So when looking at market awareness levels in todays landscape, we have to consider a few things:
#1 - Unaware: Is still a very real category. And it's why it can dominate on social platforms. Your goal is to still make people aware of a problem they aren't consciously thinking about.

#2 - Problem Aware: is also still a real category.. BUT, your copy is not to identify the problem (that's unaware) it's to make the prospect understand that they have a problem worth solving. "You dramatize the need vividly so the prospect realizes how badly they need the solution"  - Eugene

#3 - Solution Aware: People who are aware of the solutions that exists for their problem, they just aren't convinced which one will solve it the best. You can start ads at this solution level without raising their existing beliefs on specific products they may have already seen or researched.
The difference between Solution Aware and Product aware is that the person who is solution aware is essentially still considering all of the different types of products to solve their problem
The people who are product aware know what product they want to solve their problem.
EXAMPLEProblem: Dog is peeing in the house when i leave
What do I do? --> I search how to fix dog peeing in the house when i leave
Solutions: Get pee pads, put the dog on meds, leave the dog outside, get a dog trainer, etc.
Now that I'm aware of all the solutions, I'll start to dive into the products to see which one will work best for me.

#4 - Product Aware: People are aware of your types of product & it's category, but they aren't completely aware of all YOUR product does, they aren't convinced it does it well, and they aren't convinced it's right for them.
EXAMPLEProblem Aware: Dog is peeing in the house every time I leave
What do I do? --> I search how to fix dog peeing in the house when I leave
Solution Aware: Get pee pads, put the dog on meds, leave the dog outside, get a dog trainer, etc.
Product Aware: Pee pads are what I want to get, but I'm not sure what one is the best
--
Product aware is biggest it has ever been and is a lot bigger than you think.
But it's also a lot more sophisticated than you think.
I can go from problem aware --> most aware in 20 minutes with tools like Amazon.
Continuing the ExampleI might Then search "best pee pads on amazon" buy those pee pads because they said that they were top rated on Amazon, but then after I used them, they still don't solve my problem
Now I might have the belief that "pee pads don't work" for my problem
Therefore, now am I NOT ONLY aware of Pee Pad products, I'm most aware of the brand that didn't work AND I now have a bias belief that pee pads don't solve this problem
So then I likely go look at other solutions.
BUT, THIS PERSON IS STILL PRODUCT AWARE OF PEE PADS.
Which is why if you can WIN at the product aware level, you will unlock massive scale.
The problem is, you likely struggle with product aware because you have no positioning (which I'm trying to help you with)

#5 - Most Aware: This one is now more prevalent then ever as well.
These people have likely seen your ads or heard of your brand before, but they may not trust that your brand specifically can actually deliver to their needs or haven't got the right offer for it.
They essentially need something to push them over the edge to buy.

lessons.name: a81f5403
lessons.title: The framework behind great hooks
lessons.description:
Hook is the #1 job of the writer.
Your hook has to be STICKY ...
When your fishing, you don't just want the fish to bite on the hook and then fall of
You want the fish to STAY on the hook so you can reel it in.
Same idea applies to your hook on ads.
You might have a great hook that gets a lot of bites
But if you can't reel it in, who cares?
Content Creators Goals:

90% retention for the first 6 seconds.Hook Must-HavesEMOTIONCURIOSITY GAPHIGH STAKESHook Example (Full Credit Adley)
“This 25-year-old kid knows exactly how I’m going to die just from this.”
An entertainment wrapper that funnels all the way down to a genetic testing kit
End of the day, it's a genetic testing kit...
But this one tells you “how you're going to die.”
It’s HOW they positioned it…
Insane example…
Made themselves a category of 1.
Hook Example:
“This is how my nonverbal toddler found his voice"
Emotion --> Hope
Curiosity  --> How did a nonverbal toddler find it's voice?
High Stakes --> Diagnosed nonverbal

Hook Example:
“ I've had four cats in my life, and I'm embarrassed to say I just learned this "
Emotion --> embarrassment
Curiosity  --> What did this authority just learn?
High Stakes --> Cat being thrown into a boat


Start in ActionDon’t over explain it, START it right in the action (even for "yap sessions")
Examples:
Somebody literally choking (visual)Authority talking about pros & cons
Have 0 backstory
We are making videos that users were NOT planning on watching
You can’t make them feel like they are missing something about you

Zero ChaosCrazy editing, too much to focus on, sensory overload, a CONFUSED brain will scroll.
Curious NOT confused.
When in doubt, dumb it down.

Understandable Without SoundStraight forward
- Adley from Viralish

lessons.name: 1104cc90
lessons.title: The 2 ways to write great hooks
lessons.description:
#1 - Make a Promise (better deliver it)
#2 - Open a Loop/create an itch (better be worth it)

Which one is MORE interesting?
Leave in the context →  Make a Promise (context = the idea is really good and interesting)
Take out the context → Open Loop

IMPORTANT TO AVOID CONFUSIONNow, before I get into the examples below, I want to make it clear that most "open loops" have some form of a promises inside of them
BUT
When you "truly make a promise" in your hook, you're essentially giving them all of the information they need, but they still want to click to see it.
Again, if something is INTERESTING enough for people to stay and watch, just say it.
Opening a loop is more focused on WITHHOLDING information.
Meaning we don't give enough for people to fully know whats going on, so they have to keep watching.

Make a PromiseHe covered his floor with 100,000 Pennies --> "This is interesting... Click"
Context = the 100,000 pennies = Promise (I better see 100,000 pennies)
Open Loop version --> You'll never believe what he covered his floor with

Lighter VS Lollipop --> "This is interesting... Click"
Context = lighter & the lollipop = Promise (I better see a lighter VS a lollipop)
Open Loop version --> I can't believe this only takes 0.1 seconds

Making the world's hardest omelette without beating the eggs (day 253) --> "This is interesting... Click"
Context = making an omelette without beating = Promise (I better see an omelette made without beating)
Open Loop version --> The omelette technique that took 253 days to master

The king of making promises (credit: Harry Dry)

Open LoopsTake out the context. Try to "delete" the product.
It goes from, "This is interesting" --> "Whats going to happen next?"
Which shoes will protect your feet the most? (high stakes jumping on a bed of nails) --> Which ones actually will?
Promise version --> Jumping on a bed of nails in crocs

Watch out for these ingredients when buying shampoo --> What ingredients do I need to look out for?

Watch what eggs to do to your old dogs body --> What do eggs do?

Promise/Open Loops CombinedHere's how to bathe your dog without water (juxtaposition) --> "How is she going to do that?"
But also promises you will see how to bathe a dog without water (context)

How ice cubes clean a scorching pan (juxtaposition) --> "This is interesting... Click"
Context = the ice cubes cleaning the scorching pan = Promise (I better see it clean this)
But also has an open loop of "how it cleans it"

Hands down the coolest kid's craft --> "What is the craft?"
Promise --> This better be a cool kids craft...


Some are clear promises, some are clear open loops, some mix both together.

The power of open loops in copy --> 100% Full Credit Harry Dry.

Credit:
Adley - Viralish
Harry Dry

lessons.name: ca93f4b0
lessons.title: 1️⃣ - How to write open loops
lessons.description:
It is an information gap that the reader/watcher wants to "fill" in their head
You create an open "task" in their mind, and they want to close that task
Again, you are WITHHOLDING information to create intrigue.
You need to create an itch/open a loop in the first 3 seconds
Then do NOT scratch it/close that loop until the final 3 seconds.

#1 - Open Loops: JuxtapositionJuxtaposition --> 2 things together that SHOULD NOT go together
"Great Copywriting is just a search for juxtaposition”
- Eugene Schwartz
How can you create a HOT tap and a COLD tap
We only know HOT because of COLD

Examples:
How a homeless person became a millionaire (We have a point A. (broke) → Point Z (millionaire), which creates a gap and AKA opens a loop)I quit the gym and lost 20 lbs (how does someone quit the gym and lose weight??)“The natural deodorant that performs like a toxic one” (natural + toxic)"Remember everything, organize nothing" (everything + nothing)"14+ Hours, no swelling" (we have point A (14 hours) --> Point Z (no swelling) which creates a gap for how that's possibleJuxtaposing images & copy (tree --> receive a heart?)Juxtaposing clips & copy (pouring water in suit case? --> keeping valuables safe?)
Juxtaposing with just imagery (goat --> in house?)Juxtaposition piques our interest because we have to pay attention to things that are unfamiliar.
"The strongest coffee"
There is no HOT & COLD.
There is no juxtaposition.
Everybody says this

But when deathwish copy rewrites:
"Live with a death wish"
- Death Wish Coffee

There is a hot & cold (live & death)
There is a juxtaposition
No other coffee brand can say this
Juxtapositions create space... That SPACE is what the reader wants to CONTINUE watching for.
#2 - Open Loops: Through Fear ETHICALLYYou can also stop hooks by focusing on triggering more of the subconscious.
The subconscious is on conscious alert to make sure that we stay alive and that we are safe
It's why you could be completely focused on something, but as soon as you hear a loud noise
You immediately alert to what is going on, and your survival instincts kick in
You can trigger this side of the brain by focusing on communicating to it and instigating that there is potential danger ahead
"Watch out for these ingredients when buying shampoo" (watch out = I need to make sure I'm not in danger)"3 Red flags of vitamin deficiency in kids" (I need to watch this to make sure my kid doesn't have one of them)"What if everything you knew about dandruff is wrong?" (I need to watch this to make sure I'm not missing something)"Watch how X stops negative thing" (How does this stop this?)
My Favorite Hook Types:
"Watch out for X"
"Red flags your X"

#1 RULE --> DON'T. BE. A. PIECE. OF. SHIT.

#3 - Open Loops: Do The OppositeIf everybody is doing the same thing
If everybody is positioning the same way
Just do the OPPOSITE
Axe: Targeting Men (get girls)
Dial: Targeting Men (mansuit)
Irish Springs: Targeting men (keep skin clean, get girls)
Old Spice: Targeting women (the man your man could smell like)

lessons.name: dd573d57
lessons.title: 2️⃣ - How to write a bridge
lessons.description:
Once your hook has 1 goal, grabbed their attention.
Your bridge also has 1 goal, keep their attention
The goal of a great bridge is to MAKE SURE we keep audience hooked in & engaged.
The bridge is the most important part to decide whether or not someone keeps watching or they drop off.
Bridges can also be sometimes great hooks.
This strategy is called in media res (more down below)
And a lot of times just by cutting the hook out and starting straight in the action can lead to breakthrough ads.
One of the $1,000,000 ads we made (single ad spent $1M) was actually just an in-media res hook (aka a bridge hook) where we cut off the original hook and started at the bridge.
Sometimes you don't need to set up the bridge, and the bridge itself can be the hook.


6 Ways To Write Effective Bridges:#1 - Introduce the mechanism (Bridge back to benefit)
#2 - Escalate the problem (relatability/emotion)
#3 - Escalate the desire (relatability/emotion)
#4 - Reposition the problem (Ideally with an authority)
#5 - Allude to new information (ideally from authority)
#6 - Setting the timeline (how long/what you will explain)

Example Bridges:#1 - Introduce the mechanism + tie back to promise (P-B-P)
Hook: if you have X, I need to show you this.
Bridge: The X MECHANISM helped me get DESIRE (CONTROL). And the Y MECHANISM helps with COMMON PROBLEM.

#1 - Introduce the mechanism + tie back to promise (P-B-P)
Hook: Watch how this [PRODUCT] stops [PROBLEM]
Bridge: First, this [PRODUCT] has a [NEW MECHANISM]. And the [NEW MECHANISM] is what actually stops [PROBLEM] and causes [VISUAL SOLUTION OF PROBLEM]

#2 - Escalate the problem (relatability/emotion)

Hook:  What if everything you knew about dandruff was wrong?
Bridge: There's an uncomfortable truth about those embarrassing white flakes on your shoulders, and it's way grosser than you think.

#2 - Escalate the problem (relatability/emotion)
Hook: Watch if you use X
Bridge: I thought I was being a X AVATAR, but after Y MONTHS, PROBLEM WAS STILL HAPPENING, and now PROBLEM IS EVEN WORSE

Bridge: Only wanting chicken nuggets? Red flag. Sugar cravings? Red flag. Low appetite? Red Flag.

Bridge:  You're probably dreading tomorrow's nail battle as much as your dog is, but what if I showed you dogs actually falling asleep during trims.

#3 - Escalate the desire (relatability/emotion)

Bridge: If you smell like this... I'm definitely coming over.

Example of in-media-res (Bridges that are hooks)REMEMBER,  Ideally your bridge has some kind of context around what your talking about, other this will likely not be effective.

lessons.name: 44642f2d
lessons.title: 3️⃣ - How to prevent/handle objections in writing
lessons.description:
How to identify objections:Product Market Objections ("Tried before, didn't work" / "Category doesn't work")Reassigning - Blame the real villain, not the categoryFacts - Specific differentiation from what failedBecause - Explain why this time is differentReversals - Position as the reason you made itWhat are customers objections about the products?

Claim Objections ("Don't believe your promise" / "Sounds too good to be true")Facts - Visual, falsifiable, ownable proofBecause - Mechanism that validates the claimReassigning - Only if explaining why past claims failedReversals - ❌ Doesn't address skepticismWhat are the objections on your claims?

Avatar Objections ("I'm not X enough" / "This won't work for ME")Reversals - "You don't have to be X"Because - "Works because it doesn't require X"Reassigning - "You're not broken, the villain is Y"Facts - ❌ Doesn't address internal beliefWhat are their personal objections? (their own beliefs)
How to handle objections:Writing To Sophistication (Eugene)Stage 1-2: "Does this even work?"  
Due to the infancy of the market, you'll need to handle objections with direct proof and clear mechanism explanation.
Stage 3-4: "How is yours different?" 
They've tried shit before. The objection is no longer if the product will work, it's "I don't believe these types of products work". You handle this with new mechanism & authority to reframe why past failures weren't their fault (See below)
Stage 5: "This isn't for me"
They're skeptical of everyone. The objection is no longer if the product does the job, it's about if this product aligns with their identity. Make the copy about WHO they are, not what you're selling. Describe them so accurately they can't object.

#1 - Writing With Facts (Harry + Hopkins)People can deny claims. But when you simply state facts that imply the claim, you allow the prospect to conclude you're better.
When you write with matters of facts over matters of opinion, a lot of objections die because you're not making arguable claims.
Questions to Ask:
Can they prove you wrong? 
"Delicious cookies" --> Yes they can (Says who? You? Ofcourse they are delicious) 
"Cookies that have sold out 43 times" --> Those must be some damn good cookies

#2 - Writing Reversals (Caples)Whatever their biggest objections are, make THAT your selling point. You're not fighting the objection, you're agreeing with them and then solving it. You show how your product was designed specifically for people with that objection.
Example: Grüns
Your claim: The easiest way to get your kids to take their greens 
Their Objection: My kids will know their greens and won't like them (Avatar)
Your response: Kids know their greens and still love them!
Example: Red light therapy mask
Your claim: This mask will tighten your skin 
Their objection: My skin is too damaged (Avatar) 
Your response: Tightens even the most damaged skin.

#3 - Writing With Because (Cialdini)People are more open to believing claims with reasons attached. If you've made a claim, provide a reason for it. The "because" creates a mini proof-bridge.
Example: Mushroom Coffee
Your claim: Our Mushroom Coffee tastes like real coffee 
Their Objection: I've tried mushroom alternatives, they don't taste like real coffee (Product)
Your response: This coffee actually taste like the real thing because we use decaf java bean extract. It has all the same coffee flavor, without the caffeinated crash.
Example: Easy to clean humidifier
Your claim: This is the world's easiest-to-clean humidifier
Their Objection: It can't be that easy to clean? (Claim)
Your response: It's so easy to clean because it's made of stainless steel so you can just and you can just throw it right in the dishwasher.
#4 - Reassigning The ObjectionWith this technique you're giving them permission to try again by reassigning or redirecting the objection and putting the blame elsewhere. You are removing the blame from the original thing that created the objection & placing it on a different target.
Example: Gut Health Supplement
Your claim: This probiotic actually works 
Their objection: I've taken probiotics before and nothing changed (Product)
Your response: Most probiotics fail because they die in your stomach acid before reaching your intestines. These survive because of the delayed-release capsule, which is why clinical studies show 8x better colonization rates.
New Target = The capsules were the issue, not the probiotics
Example: Premium Dog Food
Your claim: Your dog will actually eat this 
Their objection: I've tried premium dog foods. My dog still had digestive issues (Product) 
Your response: If you check the ingredients on other premium dog brands, a lot still use grain fillers that dogs can't digest. This is 80% real meat with zero grain fillers.
New Target = Grain fillers were the issue, not premium dog food

#5 - Writing With Gradualization (Eugene)"The best objection handling is preventing the objection from ever forming in the prospect's mind."
Build a "stream of acceptances" so the reader never has breathing space to question.
Techniques:
Promise-Belief-Promise Variation (PBP): Every sentence of promise followed by proof/verification/documentation
After you make a promise, provide proof.Paragraph Parallelism (PP): Use accepted statement structure to borrow acceptance for fresh claims
When you get someone to agree to a statement, you can leverage that statement to take a step closer to your next one.Repetition of Proof (RP): "These experts found... These experts found..."
This is where authority, facts, and data come into play. Leverage them to pull away the bias from you and act as the one sharing the information.Example: Grüns
You know greens are good for you. (Accepted truth - no objection )
You also know you should be taking them daily. (Building on acceptance)
But here's what stops you: the taste. The texture. The 30 seconds of shaking that still leaves clumps. (Naming their real objection before they think it)
That's why 74% of greens buyers quit within 3 weeks. (Proof - not their fault, it's the product category)
We fixed all three problems. (Promise - now they're ready to hear how)
These greens are in gummy form. (Mechanism - specific, falsifiable)
The taste? Actual freeze-dried strawberries and monk fruit. Not "natural flavors." (Proof through specificity)
In 60-day tests, 89% took them every single day. (Proof at moment they're wondering "will I actually stick with this?")
That's 3x the adherence rate of leading greens powders.
Because the best greens formula in the world is worthless if it's sitting in your cabinet. (Restating the problem they now believe you've solved)
Example Carepod:
https://f.io/4XyBmaCE

How to Handle Price Objections:Never defend price. Reframe what they're buying.
Method 1: Daily Breakdown + Comparison
Structure: "Not $X, it's $Y per day" or "Not $X, it's the same as a cup of coffee"
Gut Health: "$59/month = $1.97/day. Less than a bottle of kombucha.
Weight Loss: "$47/month = $1.57/day. Your Starbucks habit costs $6/day and adds pounds. This removes them."
Method 2: Expensive Cost Comparison
Structure: "Compared to [expensive alternative], this is nothing"
Hair Loss: "Transplants cost $15,000 and don't stop future loss. This is $49/month and addresses the enzyme causing it."
Dog Food: "$80/month for proper nutrition VS $1,000s later in supplements & vet bills"
Method 3: Desire Reframe
Structure: You're not selling the product, you're selling the outcome/identity.
Weight Loss: "You're not buying a powder. You're buying the ability to wear the clothes in the back of your closet again."
Hair Loss: "You're not buying a treatment. You're buying confidence in photos. You're buying the ability to finally leave the house without your hat"

lessons.name: 30d70b9a
lessons.title: 4️⃣ - How to pitch without rejection
lessons.description:
Before you make any pitch, you have to:
#1 - Ensure you delivered your payoffYou've given your 4 reasons whyYou've filled the curiosity gap.You've delivered on your promise.
Great payoffs USUALLY lead to great shares because payoffs make people:
Feel like they got valueFeel like they discovered something new (they're first)Feel like it could help someone they know
Side-Tip:
Your payoff can be also be your HOOK (Show the payoff/desire outcome in the hook, then explain how it got there)
Payoff: "Laundry detergents have harsh chemicals"
Rest of the video is explains it.

Payoff: "💩 has never felt this good"
Rest of the video is explains it.


#2 - Ensure you've established belief.You've built relatabilityYou've provided a new mechanismYou've provided proofYou've leveraged authoritiesYou've prevented/handled objections
Once you have done both of those, only then does it make sense for you to pitch. But the way that you pitch matters.
Examples of how to pitchWhen it comes to pitching, a lot of brands nowadays choose to take the non-biased approach and make "recommendations" rather than pitches.
However, if you have a real purpose behind your company, and a real reason behind your brand, you can share those reasons directly as a company.
Something that is also very important is how to transition into the pitch
NOTE* Of course for offer pitches and most aware style ads, we're pitching directly in the ad.
Transition patterns:
"Now here's the thing..." (shifts from education to recommendation)"So if you're wondering where to start..." (invitation, not push)"The one caveat is..." (natural objection that leads to product)"Here's what I did..." (personal story bridge)"Now everyone in my comments asked about this" (personal story bridge)Examples: Not From Company
Non-urgent
"An AUTHORITY recommend me to try this""If you want the one I'm using, it's from X brand""I found these from X company""I chose this brand's because X reason, Y reason, Z reason""Over X people switched to this brand because of X""If you're curious, link below"Urgent:
"The ones linked below are viral and keep selling out""This one is selling out fast, but it's linked below""I think they have a huge sale going on right now but not sure how long it will last"
Examples: From Company
Non Urgent:
"We started X brand because of Y issue""If you want to try our products, we do have X guarantee"Urgent
"We do have a sale active right now, while supplies last""We have sold out X times now, so if you want to try X, link is below"
Credit: Adley - Viralish

lessons.name: 900fec85
lessons.title: How to raise the stakes
lessons.description:
People care MORE when there is MORE at stake.
Stakes = What you stand to GAIN or LOSE
The bigger the potential gain or loss, the more people will pay attention
Gameshow for $10,000 VS Mr.Beasts $5,000,000 on the line = high stakes
Poker hand for $5 VS $1,000,000 = high stakes
Proposing on a beach VS proposing in a stadium = High stakes
After writing ad, ask yourself, how can we have more at stake? How can we create more drama? How can we make the ad feel like a big deal?
5 Ways to Raise Stakes
#1 - MAKE IT BIGGER (escalation)
Increase the scale, severity, or extremity.
Examples:
Dog pees in house → dog ruins $10,000 hardwood floorsKid struggles to talk → Kid is diagnosed as nonverbalincreased energy → Wake up feeling like you could run through a wallThe internet is raising my kids →  I don't want the Kardashians raising kids
"Internet" (not visual, not extreme) →  Kardashians (very visual, very extreme)The question: Can I make the problem/solution more extreme?

#2 - ADD WITNESSES
Introduce an audience, authority, or social pressure.
Examples:
Dog pees in house → dog pees in front of our landlordFishing under a bridge → Cop found us fishing under a bridgeLosing the weight → Your kids watch you do the hard thing and learn they can tooThe question: Who's watching? Who will see if this goes right/wrong?

#3 - MAKE IT URGENT
Add time pressure or point of no return.
Examples:
Improves teeth → The damage is happening RIGHT NOWDog pees in house → every pee in the house reinforces that behaviorNow is the time to do it → You're at the PERFECT age to do this (gets harder every year)The question: Why does this matter RIGHT NOW?

#4 - MAKE IT PERMANENT
Show that damage can't be undone or opportunity won't come back.
Examples:
Dental issues → LIFETIME of problemsDental issues → LIFETIME of people complimenting you on your smile.Cheap razors → Ingrown hairs create PERMANENT scarring/dark spotsHigh-quality wallets → Your grandkids will use this walletThe question: What's lost/gained forever if they don't act?

#5 - MAKE IT COST MORE
Add financial, relational, time-based, or emotional price tags.
Examples:
Crashes from coffee → every morning coffee is robbing you of 3 hoursSnoring issue → Your wife sleeps in another room (intimacy gone)Dental Issue → Cosmetic surgery can costs $1,000s
The question: What's this REALLY costing them? (money, relationships, time)

Ad Specific Examples:DNA Kit
This DNA kit tells you your heritage --> Low stakes
This DNA kit could predict when you might die --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
You can find out when you might DIE? (MAKE IT BIGGER)

Relationship Song
I got a custom song for my wife --> Low stakes
My wife thinks I forgot her birthday --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
Forgetting your wife's birthday could cost your relationship (MAKE IT COST MORE)



Dog Powder:
Dog powder helps clean your dogs teeth --> Low stakes
Not cleaning your dogs teeth sets them up for a lifetime of dental issues --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
Your dog can have a LIFETIME of issues (MAKE IT PERMANENT)

EDC Kit:
EDC kit helps you draw fast --> Low stakes
EDC kit helps you draw fast in an emergency --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
This is needed for EMERGENCY (MAKE IT URGENT)

Fishing Coozie
This is a coozie you can fish with --> Low stakes
Cop found us under a bridge agian  --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
He got caught by the police (ADD WITNESSES)

Veneers:
Putting on veeners with teeth that are crooked --> Low stakes
Putting on veeners when you have 2 teeth  --> High stakes
What creates the stakes? 
How BAD her teeth are and the fact she is missing so many (MAKE IT BIGGER)

lessons.name: 358c82f4
lessons.title: How to use metaphors/similes/analogies
lessons.description:
metaphors/similes/analogies strategy
You use them to:
Provide context for the brain to draw fromMake complex science simpleReframe why old solutions failedMetaphors:
Make a symbolic comparison saying one thing is another.
"A glove for your foot"
Similes:
Make direct a comparison between two things using "like" or "as".
"Fits your foot like a glove"
Analogies
Show a relationship between relationships. They follow the pattern: A is to B as C is to D
"A sock is to a foot as a glove is to a hand"
^ The problem is we're not doing poetry.
So my definition (and most non poet's definition) is when you combine metaphors and similes together to make a statement like the following:
"This shoe fits your foot like a glove fits your hand"
Not a great example, so here is one more relatable
"Trying to write winning ads without copywriting fundamentals, is like trying to fly a plane without a license"

The metaphor version requires an extra mental step, but all versions allow our brain to compare to something it knows and is familiar with to create an association with your product.


Examples: RedBull
"Red Bull Gives You Wings"
Metaphor for Energy
Wings = Energy


Examples: Mcdonalds
"Tastes like a million dollars"
Simile for it tastes GREAT
Million dollars = a good thing


Examples: HarveyTiles
Analogy for the importance of using these tiles
"Like a hospital without doctors"
Hospital without doctors would not be a good thing, just like how not having harveytiles would be a bad thing

Examples: Apple
"Test Drive a Macintosh"
Metaphor for the experience of using a Macintosh
Test Drive = Premium experience

Examples: Apple
Similes for the experience of using a Macintosh
(you can spot them all)


Examples: Heinz
"No one grows ketchup like heinz"
Visual metaphor for it's made with real tomatoes
Line + Visual = Quality ingredients + category dominance

Fun Example: Citroën
Simile for the experience of driving a Citroën

lessons.name: 303cb46b
lessons.title: How to write with labels & customer language
lessons.description:
One of the biggest mistake copywriters make is writing in "copywriter language" instead of customer language.
You shouldn't use a thesaurus to sound smarter.
You should use customer quotes to sound more like them.
Your potential customers already have words for their problems, desires, and identities.
When you use THEIR words instead of yours, two crucial things happen:
Trust - You're speaking their dialect. You're one of them, not selling themAttention - Their brain lights up when it sees familiar language (my people)There are 2 great ways you can leverage this idea for your copywriting.

#1 - Using Labels: Direct callouts in your hookLabels: What are the “Names” prospects have given themselves/identify as. What terms do they “own”?
When you're able to leverage labels and use the terms and nicknames that they use and identify with, you're able to grab their attention because they say, "oh, that is me".
It is relatable
People LOVE to own terms and label themselves because:
It's their identity (ego)It builds a sense of community (others are in my tribe)The brain loves labels (makes it easy to communicate)You can either FIND labels:
"sohm" --> stay at home mom
"ecombro" --> you know this one
"night owl" --> person who stays up late
"grinder" --> Person who works really hard
"Wasband" --> an ex husband
Or you can create your own
(this requires adoption, but when done correctly, can crush)
Peanut Butter Example from Sarah Levinger
"Creamunchy" (not creamy, not crunchy, creamunchy)
And now people are adopting this term
"Labubu"
Or if you're a knock off girly, you're a
"Lafufu"
Look at your mechanisms and ask, how can I create a new label for something?

#2 - Word Swapping: Changing "copywriter" words to "customer" wordsLook for the generic & polished copywriter words throughout your copy and replace them with the rough, specific language your customers actually use.
Generic copywriter language:
"Stressed out""Looking for a solution""Lose weight""Revolutionary product"Customer language (extracted from reviews/research):
"Completely fried""Desperate to find something that actually works""Get rid of this muffin top""Lifesaver"When you swap words copy feels native, not salesy.
Make a bank of "customer words" or "customer sayings" and add them into your copywriting tool kit.

Example Of Labels: Ridge Wallet
Label: Millennials
Example Of Labels: Manta Sleep
Label: Light Sleeper

Example Of Labels: Uncommon Goods
Label: History Nerds
Example Of Labels: Thrive Cosmetics
Label: Brown-eyed girls

Example Of Labels: Loop
Label: Gamers

How To Find Labels + Customer Langauge:One of the most interesting places to find Labels is actually on urban dictionary. In the prompt below, you will be able to find the instructions to tell Claude to go and find labels for you on there.
The second prompt that I have is for Claude to scour the internet for other customer language and labels that exist in reviews and on other websites like Reddit.
But remember, while doing manual research & building avatars, you can ALSO be jotting done specific terms & labels you see.
If you "don't recognize something" that probably means you should jot it down.
Prompts For Claude:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DSuZsQFbTIBPKoIa0FcHh9RiHegybv5lhIV22LwsxHo/edit?usp=sharing

lessons.name: f952bb0e
lessons.title: How to write unaware ads (hooks)
lessons.description:
Unaware ads appeal to the largest market, but are the hardest to create.
Which is why when you crack them, they can become your most scalable ads that convert the largest % of the market.
As indicated by the diagram above, nearly 60%+ (depending who you considered can be sold) are sitting in the unaware stage.
Unaware ads target people who are not actively seeking a solution because they either:
Don't recognize they have a problemDon't realize a new way to satisfy their specific desireThese are the people, to quote Eugene:
"who are logical prospects for your product and yet, in their own minds, are hundreds of miles away from accepting that product."
By identifying with our prospect in the hook, they will feel as they are watching or reading a piece of our content and through that content become aware of the problem that exists, or become aware of a way to satisfy their desire that they were not aware of.


Characteristics of an Unaware Ad1. It's CamouflagedIt doesn't look, feel, or sound like an ad. It looks like:
Educational/entertaining piece of contentStory someone is sharingInformation they genuinely want to consumeBut: Camouflage ≠ Unaware.
You can camouflage a problem-aware ad too. The difference is what you're camouflaging around.

2. Identity Over ProductThe hook must be their headline, their problem, their state of mind, even if they don't know it's a problem yet. You're giving words to something they feel but haven't articulated.
When it comes to unaware ads, it is important to understand:
Price means nothing to them.The name of your product means nothing to them.What your product does, what benefit it provides, or the problem it solves all means nothing to them.With starting with unaware ads, you have to forget about your product and concentrate on your prospect's identity.
Your hook & your headlines purpose is to sell the remainder of the ad itself.

3. The Sequence (at least how it should be)Unaware → Grab their attention with an identity driven hook/headlineProblem Aware → Make them aware of a desire or a problem/future problem they will haveSolution Aware → Show them what types of solution existsProduct Aware → Position your product as the one that solves it the best for themMost Aware → Make them an offer that makes an impulse buying decision, easy.

Eugene's Examples For Unaware Ads:Giving words to a hidden dream - The University of the nightExploiting a hidden fear - Why men crack...Leading into an unacceptable problem by starting with a universally accepted image - Within the curve of a woman's armUsing a common objection to capture a greater market - Why haven't TV owners been told these facts?Projecting an ultimate triumph that prospects will identify with - They laughed when I sat down at the piano, but when I started to play!⎯Projecting the result of a problem that avoids rejection that a direct statement would cause - Often a bridesmaid, but never a brideProjecting the result of an accomplishment to attract people who don't want to put in the effort - Here's an extra $50, Grace.Evolve Simplified Strategies For Unaware Ads:The Openers:1. Hidden FearTap into fears everyone shares but don't talk about daily.
Hook structure: Lead with the fear, tell a story around it, then bridge to your solution.

2. Hidden DesireTap into desires everyone shares but don't talk about daily.
Hook structure: Lead with the desire, tell a story around it, then bridge to your solution.

3. Did You KnowTaps into the minds genuine curiosity.
Hook structure: Lead with a question, stat, or story that can be bridged to the problem

4. DebateTaps into the minds love for taking sides. Standing for something
Hook structure: Lead with an open-ended question/comparison, bridge to the problem.

lessons.name: ec92b866
lessons.title: The laws of story telling
lessons.description:
Harry's 5 laws of storytelling:
No conflict, no storyNo people, no storyNo buts and so's, no storyNo ordinary, no storyIf you start explaining, no story
Evolvified laws of storytelling:
No conflict, no storyNo change, no storyNo stakes, no storyNo buts and so's, no storyNo people, no storyNo ordinary, no storyIf you start explaining, no story
No people, no storyStories are about people
Taking a customer review and turning it into a storytelling ad
Quote:
“Started this product in October when chemo was wrapping up. My hair isn't falling out anymore. Every day I see more hair coming back, and that I contribute solely to your shampoo bars ”
Ad:
https://www.facebook.com/100064210566845/posts/1210299814453693
Another example:
Product: Tshirt blanket - This is a blanket made from t-shirts (no people)
Product + People: This blanket is from my son's shirts and is a memory blanket 
https://www.facebook.com/100064683847383/posts/1154535703379214

No buts, and so’s, no story
Your story must continue to flow from piece to piece
…..
But
…..
But
….
So
"But" changes direction in the story
"So" advances the story
IMPORTANT:
You're not always actively writing the words "but" and "so"
It’s between the lines
If the word “and” is in between your sentences, you don’t have a story, you have a shopping list.

No ordinary, no story (needs to be relatable)
It's easier to make something small feel big than the other way around.
You don't need to make it "BIG" in actual, you just want to make it feel small
It's actually better if you just start small and you can show how this small thing is BIG.
Examples
Laifen: "Billions of negative ions" VS "How to make curls"
Much simpler to answer how to make curls and make it a big thing VS bragging about 1 billion ions. Much harder to simplify that idea for how it benefits the customer

Project Repat: "Million shirts turned into blankets" VS "Send use your old shirts"
Much simpler to answer how to a couple of shirts into a life time of memories (big thing) VS bragging about MILLIONS of shirts.
1,000,000 shirts is agian, much harder to simplify for how it benefits the customer

If you start explaining, no story
Every time you explain something, just delete it and give an example.
The example will explain more than you can.
"People will steal your luggage because zippers aren't secure enough"
Example:



MASSIVE CREDIT AGAIN:
- Harry Dry
I want to take a second  to make a comment about how ridiculously knowledgeable Harry is.
You guys have no idea (well you probably do) how much game I have learned from him.
As a result I have been able to apply his principles to not only make our business better but now to help all of you as well.
I need to make it very clear that he is the mastermind behind this, and I'm simply passing along his teachings into "ecom".

lessons.title: The storytelling arcs/plots
lessons.description:
Christopher Booker argues that all stories fall into 7 categories in his book:
The Seven Basic Plots: Why We Tell Stories
And as much as these plots are great frameworks
They are NOT something that is fully needed.
The things we have discussed above + the combination of excessive knowledge on your category, you have what you need to write great stories
With that said
The reason I am choosing to cover these is because they can be GREAT for iterations on angles of winning ads and identify what specific "plots" might be resonating with your avatar.
ps. In typical Spencer fashion I have added 2 more for ads specifically.

Overcoming the Monster
Problem → fight → win

The enemy is the focus. The win is the removal of pain, not chasing a dream.
Mini story:
“For years, my energy would crash by 2 p.m.
I tried caffeine, powders, even prescriptions.
Nothing worked for long.
This was the first thing that actually stopped the crash.”Extended:
Another example of "problem, fight, win" can be seen as "PAS" (problem, agitate, solution) or even more escalated is fichtean curve where the problems compile.
Problem → New Problem → Bigger problem → Even Bigger problem → Solution to all
Fichtean curve stories are escalating and relentless, but it can work great as there is no downtime which means no boredom. Attention stays locked in & the solution becomes that much greater & more powerful.Rags to Riches (Hero's journey)
Low point → Struggle → Breakthrough → Success

This isn’t about beating one problem — it’s about becoming a new person.

Mini story:
“I used to wake up exhausted no matter how much I slept.
I planned my day around naps and coffee.
Now I wake up clear-headed and focused.
I honestly don’t recognize the old version of me.”Extended:
People love heroes, but they love heroes even more who are relatable. 

If you can create a hero that was just like them, that went through and did the thing and now has the better life as a result using your process, it can help show them what they want is possible. But again, it needs to be relatable. The other person needs to see themselves as the "same person" as the hero to actually be effective. 

Spider-Man doesn't start out as this stud who has everything. 

He starts out with a family member passing away, with his life going to shit, and then all of a sudden he becomes this hero. 

That relatability is what makes it such a powerful superhero int he movies.
It's what also makes them powerful in ads.In Media Res
Important moment/action → Discovery → Reinforcing Win

Start in the middle of the action to capture attention immediately.
Provide the additional context and fill in the points after

Mini story:
“It's 3pm and I just crushed my biggest task of the day with no brain fog, no caffeine crash, nothing.
I used to be useless by this time. 
That's when I realized: this energy thing actually works.
I'd been chasing the wrong solutions for years. 
Now every afternoon feels like a win."The Quest
Goal → Obstacles → Discovery → Win

The hook is aspirational, not desperate.
The product helps reach a desired state, not escape a monster.

Mini story:
“I’ve always wanted steady energy all day — no crashes, no burnout.
I didn’t want stimulants or shortcuts.
After digging into how energy actually works, I found this.
This is the first time my days feel the way I always wanted them to.”Voyage & Return
Normal → Chaos → Realization → Better normal

This story says: "I tried the extreme path so you don’t have to."
Very powerful for skeptical buyers.

Mini story:
“I went all-in trying to fix my energy.
Biohacks, extreme routines, supplements stacked on supplements.
It actually made things worse.
Once I stripped it back to this one simple change, everything stabilized.”Rebirth
Stuck → wake-up → transformation

No enemy. No grind.
Just a moment of awareness that unlocks change.

Mini story:
“I thought feeling tired all the time was just part of adulthood.
Then I made one small change.
Suddenly my mornings felt easier.
That’s when I realized how long I’d been running on empty.”Confusion (aka Comedy)
Misunderstanding → Insight → Clarity

Along the lines of: “I misunderstood the problem or made the wrong conclusion and now I fixed it”

Mini story:
“I kept buying products for energy.
Turns out energy wasn’t the problem.
Once I fixed this one thing, everything else worked better.
Wish I knew this sooner.”
#2:
“I thought I needed more energy.
So I kept buying energy products.
Turns out that wasn’t the issue at all.
Once I fixed this, everything else started working.”Tragedy
Downward spiral. Also know as a decline without redemption

This one specifically is not for DTC as it actually ends in a tragedy, and all of our ads are to be more positive, not negative

 this is previously used in companies like: Anti-smoking campaigns, Anti-drunk driving ads, Environmental campaigns (“If we don’t act, this is the future.”), Some charity / nonprofit ads (starving, abuse, addiction) 

The goal isn’t conversion
The goal is fear, awareness, or behavior prevention

So instead we create our own called:The Two Paths
Shows consequences and a way forward. 
Great for explainer-style ads, voiceovers, and “talking head” creatives where the goal is to shift direction, not dramatize pain.Mini story:“Most people keep pushing through fatigue the same way every day.
Over time, that just leads to more crashes and burnout.
You don’t have to keep going down that path.
When you support energy the right way, days start to feel steady again.”
#2 (higher intensity)
“If you keep pushing through fatigue with caffeine, here’s what usually happens.
The crashes get harder.
Focus gets worse.
And energy never really stabilizes.
There is another path.
When you support energy the right way, days stop swinging up and down.”This strategy is also known as the "Pixar Framework" but the idea is to future paced the ad.
It talks about what happens and shows how things progress.
If you want to see a masterclass on this + experience what it feels like to tap into the emotions of your customers & have them experience EVERYTHING we have discussed above.
I'll leave this for you to watch:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-7e6g11BJc0

lessons.name: a2de288d
lessons.title: Prompts to help you storytell
lessons.description:
Brand/Market Focused:Brand Element:
Chocolate bar using all natural ingredients
Brand Ad:
“We use all natural ingredients to make a better chocolate bar for you"
^No story, nobody cares

Market Story Ad:
“Do you know what the #1 ingredient in most chocolate bars is?" I'll give you a hint, it's not Cacao..."
^ Story, people care.

Brand Story Ad:
“Can I make a better chocolate bar than Mr.Beast?"
^ Story, people care.

Another Brand Story Example:
https://www.facebook.com/61559870645603/posts/122209578932329021
^ Story, people care.

Prompts:#1 - What is something that everyone thinks is true about your product, but isn’t?
#2 - What’s something about your product that would frustrate people?
#3 - What's a story that proves your product/service is different from competitors
#4 - What made you angry that you had to create this product? (what is your enemy)
#5 - What do your competitors hope customers never figure out?
#6 - Who is this product NOT for?


Customer Focused:Find your story starters in your reviews, build from there.
Customer Quote:
"The rat-vac made it incredibly easy to solve my pest problem and gave me my garage back. It just works."
Customer Quote Ad:
^No story, nobody cares

Customer Quote Story Ad:
"Rats took over my garage. Here's how a vacuum took it back."
^ Story, people care.

Prompt:
Use this AI Prompt + your reviews to be able to find reviews that can lead to stories
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OGUHfnnGAgM5eAadg-1BLx_fFaGi0EvALOw13YvRzNo/edit?usp=sharing

lessons.title: ⭐️ Why you need to position your brand
lessons.description:
Important Update (March 23rd)After watching back the overview of the program & editing the positioning video above, I've decided to put this video in it's own section, and more importantly, put it at the end.
Positioning is a massive concept.
It's such a big concept that the authors of the positioning books I recommend SOLELY consult brands on positioning, and positioning only.
You are welcome to watch this before completing the rest program.
BUT, this is a LOT of information to take in. More importantly, to execute this properly will require you to go very deep into your brand.
So, instead of taking this head on FIRST, I'd recommend learning the strategies laid out above around copywriting, taking action on them NOW to make more winning ads, then revisiting this concept.
That said, I can't force you to listen to me lol. So choice is yours.
- Spencer


5 Simple Takeaways To Start With Positioning:
Can You Create a New Category?: Instead of competing in an existing market, can you invent a new subcategory where you have no competitors? (Apple - the smartphone, Poppi - the prebiotic sodas, Dude Wipes - sanitary wipes for men)How Can You Create Contrast?: Can you put yourself against the "status quo" and do the opposite of what everyone else is doing? (Liquid Death - Water in can, not a bottle. Shopify - for the merchants, Stoli's - vodka that is actually russion)How Can You Align With Values?: Can you align yourself with a specific belief or social caus  that use values to attract a loyal tribe while alienating others. (Comfrt  - mental health, Black Rifle Coffee - veteran rights)Who Is Your Strategic Enemy?:ho or what are you against? (Uber - against Taxis, The Farmer's Dog - against Kibble, Lalo - against ugly hair chairs)What Will You Say No To?:  What are you willing to say no to that other competitors can't?
(GEM - said no to pills, Brandy Melville - said no to tons of sizes, The Conscious Bar - said no to added sugar)Credits:
Jack TroutAl RiesLaura RiesApril DunfordHarry DryKyle Milligan

lessons.name: 42f2a88e
lessons.title: 💥 Positioning Exercise
lessons.description:
What position do you want to own?Own is the key word. 

Too many brands want to own a position that is impossible to own because someone else already owns it.

Example: A company called Richardson Merrill was trying to position in the cold remedy category head-on. But the formula developed was causing drowsiness which was a huge drawback for people taking it.

However, they took that drawback and chose to market and own a new category for night time cold remedies in the 1960s.

Also known asNyQuil. With proper positioning, that "product flaw" turned out to be pretty successful (to the tune of the founder selling for $1.55 billion in 1985).
The important thing to keep in mind, though, is it's not just about what you want.
It's also about what the customer is willing to accept.

Remember The 5 Takeaways:How Can You Create a New Category?: 
Instead of competing in an existing market, can you invent a new subcategory where you have no competitors? (Apple - the smartphone, Poppi - the prebiotic sodas, Dude Wipes - sanitary wipes for men)
How Can You Create Contrast?:  
Can you put yourself against the "status quo" and do the opposite of what everyone else is doing? (Liquid Death - Water in can, not a bottle. Shopify - for the merchants, Stoli's - vodka that is actually Russian)
How Can You Align With Values?:  
Can you align yourself with a specific belief or social cause that use values to attract a loyal tribe while alienating others. (Comfrt - mental health, Black Rifle Coffee - veteran rights)
Who Is Your Strategic Enemy?: Who or what are you against? (Uber - against Taxis, The Farmer's Dog - against Kibble, Lalo - against ugly high chairs)
What Will You Say No To?: 
What are you willing to say no to that other competitors can’t? (GEM - said no to pills, Brandy Melville - said no to tons of sizes, The Conscious Bar - said no to added sugar)

Step 1: Map The Competitive LandscapeResearch what's already in the prospect's mind:
What category are you in?Who do you compete with in that category?Who's the leader in the category and what do they stand for?What positions do competitors already own in this category?Step 2: Get Into The DetailsPath A: Can you create a new (sub)category?
Can you narrow your focus to be FIRST in something?Path B: Can you find the obvious hole?
Can't be first? Redefine who it's for or how to think about the categoryWhat are competitors unwilling to do/say/show?What inverse position can you take? (timeless vs trendy, one size vs inclusive)What can you call out that others won't? (Halo Top: eat the whole pint)What's the obvious, but no so-obivous, problem/gap no one's addressing?Step 3: Make It ConcreteDefine your strategic enemy(s):
Is it a competitor, an approach, or a belief/concept?Define what you'll say "no" to:
What will you eliminate that competitors won't?Make it visually different:
Different beats better, how can you visually stand out?
Active Exercise To Get FlowingWho do you compete against?
Who I’m Up Against				  | 		How Are You Different
Brand 1Brand 2Brand 3Brand 4
What do you do you compete against?

Ask yourself, big or small, serious or not, what are all the problems with products out there.
Product problems	  | 		How you can solve
Problem 1Problem 2Problem 3Problem 4Ask yourself, big or small, meaningless or meaningful. What is different, and how could that solve a problem?
Things that are different	  | 		Problem it could solve

The secret to establishing a successful position is to keep two things in balance:

A unique position with an appeal that's not too narrow

lessons.name: c91cc1de
lessons.title: What about AI?
lessons.description:
You don't need another copywriting prompt
There are enough of them out there
What you need is the skillset to know whats good and whats not.
AI is phenomenal at identifying
AI is phenomenal at filling in the gaps
AI is phenomenal at gathering things
But AI should never be your strategy, for now.


Now will we be optimizing a series of prompts, more than likely.
But that is for a bigger picture that I can go into clear detail at this time.

lessons.name: 4d60dae2
lessons.title: Visual words
lessons.description:
AI Prompt:
Read the following copy. Can you highlight every word or sentence that contains
a) Abstract verbs
b) Abstract nouns
c) Abstract adjectives
d) Abstract adverbs
e) Cliches
^ Credit Harry Dry
Your goal is to go from ABSTRACT to CONCRETE
Sheet of paper → and just keep writing until you go from ABSTRACT to concrete
For example, say you're writing about habits. Don't talk about
"productive routines."
That's abstract.
Write about
"waking up at 6 am to write" instead.
It's concrete/visual.

lessons.name: 2d780db7
lessons.title: Eugene's Headlines
lessons.description:
1. Measure the size of the claim
20,000 FILTER TRAPS IN VICEROY!
I AM 61 POUNDS LIGHTER…
WHO EVER HEARD OF 17,000 BLOOMS FROM A SINGLE PLANT?
2. Measure the speed of the claim
FEEL BETTER FAST!
IN TWO SECONDS, BAYER ASPIRIN BEGINS TO DISSOLVE IN YOUR GLASS!
3. Compare the claim
SIX TIMES WHITER WASHES!
COSTS UP TO $300 LESS THAN MANY MODELS OF THE LOW-PRICED THREE!
4. Metaphorize the claim
BANISHES CORNS!
MELTS AWAY UGLY FAT!
5. Sensitize the claim by making the prospect feel, smell, touch, see, or hear it
TASTES LIKE YOU JUST PICKED IT!
THE SKIN YOU LOVE TO TOUCH!
6. Demonstrate the claim by showing a prime example
JAKE LAMOTTA, 160 POUND FIGHTER, FAILS TO FLATTEN MONO PAPER CUP!
AT 60 MILES AN HOUR, THE LOUDEST NOISE IN THIS ROLLS ROYCE IS THE ELECTRIC CLOCK!
7. Dramatize the claim, or its result
HERE’S AN EXTRA $50 GRACE — I’M MAKING BIG MONEY NOW!
THEY LAUGHED WHEN I SAT DOWN AT THE PIANO — BUT WHEN I STARTED TO PLAY…
8. State the claim as a paradox
HOW A BALD-HEADED BARBER SAVED MY HAIR!
BEAT THE RACES BY PICKING LOSERS!
9. Remove limitations from the claim
SHRINKS HEMORRHOIDS WITHOUT SURGERY!
YOU BREATHE NO DUSTY ODORS WHEN YOU DO IT WITH LEWYT!
10. Associate the claim with value or people with whom the prospect wishes to be identified
MICKEY MANTLE SAYS: CAMELS NEVER BOTHER MY THROAT!
9 OUT OF 10 DECORATORS USE WUNDA-WEAVE CARPETS FOR LONG LIFE AT LOW COST!
11. Show how much work, in detail, the claim does
NOW! RELIEF FROM ALL 5 ACID-CAUSED STOMACH TROUBLES — IN SECONDS!
RELIEVES CONGESTION IN ALL 7 NASAL PASSAGES INSTANTLY!
12. State the claim as a question
WHO ELSE WANTS A WHITER WASH — WITH NO HARD WORK?
COULD YOU USE $25 A WEEK EXTRA INCOME?
13. Offer information about how to accomplish the claim
HOW TO WIN FRIENDS AND INFLUENCE PEOPLE!
HERE’S WHAT TO DO TO GET RID OF PIMPLES FAST!
14. Tie authority into the claim
BOSS MECHANIC SHOWS HOW TO AVOID ENGINE REPAIR BILLS!
HERE’S WHAT DOCTORS DO WHEN THEY FEEL ROTTEN!
15. Before-and-after the claim
BEFORE COLDENE A CHILD GOT OVER A COLD AFTER 5 DAYS OF ACHING, SNEEZING, WHEEZING, DRIPPING, SUFFERING, COUGHING, CRYING, GAGGING, SPITTING. WITH COLDENE A CHILD GETS OVER A COLD IN FIVE DAYS!
16. Stress the newness of the claim
ANNOUNCING! GUIDED MISSILE SPARK PLUGS!
NOW! CHROME PLATE WITHOUT HEAT, ELECTRICITY, MACHINERY!
17. Stress the exclusivity of the claim
OURS ALONE! PERSIAN LAMB ORIGINALS — $389.40!
ONLY GLEEM HAS GL-70 TO KEEP TEETH CLEAN ALL DAY LONG WITH ONE BRUSHING!
18. Turn the claim into a challenge for the reader
WHICH TWIN HAS THE TONI? AND WHICH HAS THE $15 PERMANENT?
DOES SHE OR DOESN’T SHE? HAIR COLORING SO NATURAL ONLY HER HAIRDRESSER KNOWS FOR SURE!
19. State the claim as a case-history quotation
LOOK MOM — NO CAVITIES!
WOULD YOU BELIEVE IT — I HAVE A COLD!
20. Condense the claim — interchange your product and the product it replaces
NOW! A RING AND PISTON JOB IN A TUBE!
POUR YOURSELF A NEW ENGINE!
21. Symbolize the claim — replace the direct statement or measurement of the claim with a parallel reality
STARTING NEXT TUESDAY, THE ATLANTIC OCEAN BECOMES ONLY ONE-FIFTH AS LONG!
22. Connect the mechanism to the claim in your headline
FLOATS FAT RIGHT OUT OF YOUR BODY!
FEEDS WASTE GAS FUMES BACK INTO YOUR ENGINE!
23. Startle the reader by contradicting the way he thinks the mechanism should work
“HIT HELL OUT OF THE BALL WITH YOUR RIGHT HAND,” SAYS TOMMY ARMOUR!
24. Connect the need and the claim in the headline
THERE IS ONLY ONE SOLUTION TO AN ADVERTISING PROBLEM: FIND THE MAN!
25. Offer information in the ad itself
WHY MEN CRACK…
WHAT EVERYBODY OUGHT TO KNOW ABOUT THIS STOCK AND BOND BUSINESS!
26. Turn the claim or the need into a case history
AUNT MEG, WHO NEVER MARRIED…
AGAIN SHE ORDERS — “A CHICKEN SALAD, PLEASE”
27. Give a name to the problem or need
WHEN YOU’RE WEARY WITH DAY-TIME FATIGUE, TAKE ALKA-SELTZER
28. Warn the reader about possible pitfalls if he doesn’t use the product
DON’T INVEST ONE CENT OF YOUR HARD-EARNED MONEY UNTIL YOU CHECK THIS GUIDE!
29. Emphasize the claim by its phraseology — by breaking it into two sentences, or repeating it, or a part of it
A MAN YOU CAN LEAN ON! THAT’S KLOPERMAN!
NOBODY BUT NOBODY UNDERSELLS GIMBEL’S!
30. Show how easy the claim is to accomplish by imposing a universally-overcome limitation
IF YOU CAN COUNT TO ELEVEN, YOU CAN INCREASE YOUR SPEED AND SKILL AT NUMBERS!
31. State the difference in the headline
THE DIFFERENCE IN PREMIUM GASOLINES IS RIGHT IN THE ADDITIVES!
32. Surprise your reader into reading that former limitations have now been overcome
SEE WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU CRUSH A HARTMAN DC-8? NOTHING!
33. Address the people who can’t buy your product
IF YOU’VE ALREADY TAKEN YOUR VACATION, DON’T READ THIS. IT’LL BREAK YOUR HEART.
34. Address your prospect directly
TO THE MAN WHO WILL SETTLE FOR NOTHING LESS THAN THE PRESIDENCY OF HIS FIRM.
35. Dramatize how hard it was to produce the claim
WHEN JENS FINISHED DESIGNING THIS CANDLEHOLDER WE HAD TO INVENT A WHOLE NEW KIND OF CANDLE.
36. Accuse the claim of being too good
IS IT IMMORAL TO MAKE MONEY THIS EASILY?
37. Challenge the prospect’s present limiting beliefs
YOU ARE TWICE AS SMART AS YOU THINK.
38. Turn the claim into a question and answer
YOU DON’T KNOW WHAT’S UNDER THE HOOD AND YOU COULDN’T CARE LESS AS LONG AS YOUR CAR RUNS SMOOTHLY. WHO SHOULD YOU SEE IF IT DOESN’T? … SOMEONE WHO CARES — UNITED DELCO.
